arms.notes: ResNet1d from src/ecs/models.py, input (B, 12, 5000) mV, 256-d embedding
arms.preprocessing: none beyond the common ingestion: (12, 5000) float32 millivolts at 500 Hz goes into the network unchanged

arms.pretraining_corpora: Harvard-Emory ECG Database, >10 million recordings; no public corpus named (arXiv:2410.04133; HF model card PKUDigitalHealth/ECGFounder)
arms.notes: Net1D per the authors' finetune_model.py; 1024-d features before the dense head; input (B, 12, 5000) at 500 Hz per config.json; load_state_dict missing=0 unexpected=0
arms.preprocessing: none beyond the common ingestion: (12, 5000) float32 millivolts at 500 Hz goes into the network unchanged; the model card's config.json asks for 500 Hz, which the canonical form already is. Not applied: the band-pass and per-record z-scoring in the authors' fine-tuning code, which their model card does not require for feature extraction

arms.pretraining_corpora: MIMIC-IV-ECG v1.0 and PhysioNet/CinC 2021 v1.0.3, the latter containing PTB-XL (github.com/bowang-lab/ECG-FM README, 'Pretrained on')
arms.notes: fairseq_signals wav2vec2_cmsc; input (B, 12, 5000) at 500 Hz; mean-pooled extract_features output
arms.preprocessing: none beyond the common ingestion: (12, 5000) float32 millivolts at 500 Hz goes into the network unchanged; the checkpoint carries its own normalisation inside fairseq_signals' extract_features, which is applied there and not here

arms.pretraining_corpora: Ribeiro/CODE, CPSC and CPSC-Extra, PTB and PTB-XL, Georgia, Chapman-Shaoxing, Ningbo, Tianchi (Hefei), Shandong Provincial Hospital (SPH), MIMIC-IV ECG (medRxiv 10.1101/2024.11.14.24317328v3, Methods - Data and Preprocessing, read 2026-08-23)
arms.notes: transformers AutoModel with the repo's hubert_ecg.py (custom code); input (B, 6000): 5 s x 12 leads flattened then decimated by 5; 768-d mean-pooled last hidden state
arms.preprocessing: zero-phase Butterworth band-pass of order 3 between 0.05 and 47.0 Hz applied per lead at 500 Hz; first 5 seconds kept; the twelve leads flattened into one sequence and decimated to 100 Hz, in that order, as the authors' dataset.py does. Not applied: the per-record rescaling to [-1, 1] the paper also describes, which would change the scale the other arms see
